title: Preparation of Hydroxy-PAAm Hydrogels for Decoupling the Effects of Mechanotransduction Cues
protocol: Place glass circular coverslips in a Petri dish.
Smear 0.1 M NaOH solution on the coverslips for 5 min.
Remove the NaOH solution and immerse coverslips with sterile ddH2O for 20 min while rocking gently.
Drain sterile ddH2O and repeat smearing with 0.1 M NaOH solution.
Remove the coverslips with sterile tweezers and place them in a new Petri dish with the activated face up.
Dry coverslips under a steady flow of high-purity nitrogen gas.
Smear a thin layer of 3-(trimethoxysilyl)propyl acrylate on the activated side of the coverslip for 1 hr.
Wash glass coverslips extensively with sterile ddH2O in three washes.
Immerse coverslips in sterile ddH2O in a new Petri dish and rock gently for 10 min.
Remove the coverslips from ddH2O with sterile tweezers with fine tips and place them in a new Petri dish with the activated face up.
Store at RT in a dry place with aluminum foil to avoid dust.
Prepare a weight of 65 mg of N-hydroxyethyl acrylamide (HEA) in a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube.
Add 1 ml of 50 mM HEPES buffer to HEA and mix using a vortexer until complete dissolution.
Add 400 µl of 40% w/w in HEPES acrylamide solution.
Add the required volume of 2% w/w in HEPES bis-acrylamide solution to reach the desired hydrogel stiffness.
Adjust with 50 mM HEPES to a final volume of 5 ml.
Mix the solution using a vortexer.
Degas the solution in a vacuum chamber for 20 min.
Filter the degased solution with a 0.2 µm pore size filter to sterilize it.
Activate circular glass coverslips (22 mm diameter) in a UV/ozone cleaner during 7 min.
Prepare 100 µl of 10% ammonium persulfate (APS) solution.
Add 2.5 µl of tetramethylenediamine (TEMED).
Add 25 µl of APS solution to the sterilized hydroxy-PAAm solution.
Mix the solution by 3 successive pipettings without introducing bubbles, under sterile conditions.
Place a 25 µl drop of the hydroxy-PAAm solution on a 25 mm coverslip.
Immediately place a 22 mm glass coverslip on top of the droplet to squeeze the hydroxy-PAAm solution.
Center the 22 mm glass coverslip with sterile tweezers and smooth out any bubbles.
Allow hydroxy-PAAM hydrogels to polymerize at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Invert manually the remaining hydroxy-PAAm solution in the Eppendorf tube to check polymerization completion.
Fully immerse coverslips with sterile ddH2O.
Introduce the edge of a razor blade between the 22 mm glass coverslips and the hydroxy-PAAm hydrogel layer to separate them carefully.
Wash hydroxy-PAAm hydrogels with sterile PBS (three exchanges).
Let the gels fully immerse in sterile PBS to maintain hydration.
Store hydroxy-PAAm hydrogels in sterile PBS at 4°C for up to 3 days.
Mix PDMS and the curing agent in a 10:1 ratio in a plastic beaker.
Mix thoroughly using a pipette for 10 minutes.
Degas the PDMS mixture under vacuum to remove air bubbles.
Place the microstructured silicon master in a Petri dish.
Cast a 10-mm thick layer of degassed PDMS mixture on it without forming bubbles.
Cure the PDMS for 2 hr at 60 °C in an oven.
Peel-off the cured PDMS layer from the silicon master in a dust-free environment.
Excise 1 cm² microstamps with a scalpel.
Place PDMS microstamps pattern-up in a Petri dish using forceps.
Place PDMS microstamps in an ethanol/water (50/50) solution and sonicate for 15 min.
Dry the stamps with a stream of nitrogen flow.
Expose the dry stamps to UV/Ozone cleaner (λ < 200 nm) for 7 min.
Under a sterile hood, place a 150 µl drop of a desired protein solution onto the microstructured surface of a PDMS stamp.
Spread the protein solution across the stamp surface with a sterile tip of a pipette toward each corner of the stamp.
Leave the protein solution to adsorb on the PDMS stamp for 60 min under a sterile hood.
Remove excess PBS from the surface of hydroxy-PAAm substrates with a low nitrogen stream under sterile conditions.
Dry carefully the structured surface of the PDMS stamp with a steady flow of high-purity nitrogen gas.
Place the protein-coated stamp in contact with the dried hydrogel surface using dressing tissue forceps.
Apply brief pressure points on the top of the PDMS stamp to ensure good contact between stamp microfeatures and the hydrogel surface.
Leave the PDMS stamp on the hydrogel surface for 1 hr at room temperature.
Gently remove PDMS stamps from hydroxy-PAAm hydrogels with dressing tissue forceps.
Wash stamped hydroxy-PAAm hydrogels by exchanging PBS three times for 10 min each exchange under sterile conditions.
Passivate non-printed zones with a sterile solution of BSA at 5 mg/ml in PBS overnight at 4 °C under gentle agitation on a rocking plate.
Wash extensively the stamped hydroxy-PAAm hydrogels by exchanging PBS three times for 10 min each exchange under sterile conditions.
Incubate coverslips in cell media for 30-45 min prior to plating cells.
Wash adherent cells cultured in a 75 cm2 culture flask with sterile PBS at 37 °C.
Detach the cells with 3 ml of trypsin-EDTA or accutase for 10 min.
Transfer pre-warmed complete growth medium into the flask containing the detached cells.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 3 min at 650 x g.
Remove the supernatant with a micropipette.
Resuspend the cells in complete culture medium at 15-20,000 cells/ml.
Add 4 ml of the cell solution to a micropatterned coverslip.
Place the cell-covered coverslip in a culture incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 1-2 hr.
Aspirate gently unattached cells.
Replace the culture medium.
Return the attached cells to the incubator.
Let the cells spread fully (3-6 hr, depending on the cell type).
